chunks: And by his chain, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu Hammam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When you come to the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), say: Peace be upon you, O Abu Abdillah. May Allah curse the one who killed you, and may Allah curse the one who shared in your blood, and the one to whom this news reached and was pleased with it. And we are free from them before Allah. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication to recite when visiting the grave of Imam Al-Husayn?
ai.summary: This narration from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* establishes the foundational formula for visiting Imam Al-Husayn’s shrine, emphasizing the theological concept of *al-bara’ah* (innocence from enemies) through specific invocations against his killers and their supporters. It reflects the Shia tradition of linking physical pilgrimage with spiritual allegiance, where reciting this supplication serves as a public declaration of loyalty to the Ahl al-Bayt and separation from their adversaries.
